entries.name: Hugging Face: Continuous batching from first principles (Nov 2025)

pad_waste_example.note: B = 8, n = 100: adding an n-token prompt to B decoding prompts under padded batching wastes (n-1)(B-1) pad tokens.

venue.note: USENIX OSDI '22 (Yu et al.). Its throughput gain is deliberately not stored (pages do not show it).

engine_loop.value: schedule → forward pass (run model, sample) → postprocess (append tokens, detokenize, check stops), every step
engine_loop.note: Gordić, "Inside vLLM" (2025-09-05), read 2026-10-07; the post folds sampling into the forward pass.

scheduler_knobs.value: per-step token budget (max_num_batched_tokens), seat cap (max_num_seqs), FCFS by default, priority classes, preemption when KV blocks run out
scheduler_knobs.note: Brief 04 §2.3 marks the knob list general knowledge (prior). The cited post confirms FCFS or priority policy and a per-step token budget; it does not name max_num_batched_tokens or max_num_seqs.

v1_preemption.note: Post: the engine "may attempt recompute preemption (swap preemption was supported in V0)". Read 2026-10-07; beyond brief 04.

default_block_size.note: PagedAttention paper §7.2: "vLLM sets its default block size as 16" (PDF read 2026-10-07); Gordić post: "Each block stores 16 tokens by default".

gain_mistral7b_a100.note: Up to 2.6x serving capacity within SLO, Mistral-7B on one A100, vs Orca and vLLM (abstract).

gain_falcon180b_8xa100.note: Up to 6.9x, Falcon-180B on 8 A100s, vs Orca and vLLM (abstract).

note_chunking.value: Smaller prefill chunks add overhead from repeated kernel launches and synchronization (GPU bubbles); MLA throughput plateaus as the prefill batch grows from 16K to 64K tokens
note_chunking.note: Post read 2026-10-07. Brief 04 §2.2 paraphrased this as "minimized chunking overheads mattered for 64K-token prefill batches"; the post's own wording is stored.

decode_gpus.note: One decode instance of 8 GB200; 16 GPUs in total.

prefill_tok_s_gpu.note: Prefill "TPGS" (tokens per GPU-second) on prefill GPUs, so it counts input (prompt) tokens. Workload 2K input / 2K output, NVFP4 MoE experts and output projection, FP8 MLA query up-projection.

decode_tok_s_gpu.note: Decode TPGS on decode GPUs, so it counts output (generated) tokens. Workload 2K input / 2K output.

kv_useful_before_pct.note: One source, not a conflict: paper §2 / Fig. 2 profiling of existing systems found only 20.4%-38.2% of KV cache memory held actual token states (2023).

waste_before_pct.note: One source, not a conflict: vLLM launch post (2023-06-20): "existing systems waste 60% - 80% of memory due to fragmentation and over-reservation". The paper's Fig. 2 (20.4-38.2% useful) is the stricter figure.

waste_after_pct_max.note: Launch post: "a mere waste of under 4%".

throughput_gain.note: One source, not a conflict: abstract, "improves the throughput of popular LLMs by 2-4x with the same level of latency" vs FasterTransformer and Orca; the paper measures throughput as served request rate at equal normalized latency (2023).

kernel_overhead_2023_pct.note: One source, not a conflict: paper §7.1, "20-26% higher attention kernel latency, compared to the highly-optimized FasterTransformer implementation" (2023 measurement).

engines.note: Brief 04 §3.2 statement (prior); the paper introduces the method but does not list the other engines.

kv_hit_rate_pct.note: 342B of 608B input tokens in 24 h hit the on-disk KV cache.

input_tokens_per_day.note: Input tokens over 24 h (168B output tokens).

avg_kv_length_tokens.note: Average KV cache length per output token.

prefill_ep.note: Routed experts EP32, MLA and shared expert DP32, over 4 nodes; 9 routed + 1 shared expert per GPU.

decode_ep.note: Routed experts EP144, MLA and shared expert DP144, over 18 nodes.

prefill_tok_s_node.note: Input tokens per second per node during prefill, including cache hits (source: "~73.7k tokens/s input (including cache hits)"). 24-hour production average.

decode_tok_s_node.note: Output tokens per second per node during decode. 24-hour production average.

cost_per_day_usd.note: At an assumed $2 per H800 GPU-hour.

gpu_hour_usd.note: The source's assumed H800 leasing cost (an accounting assumption, not a measured price).

max_throughput_tok_s_gpu.note: Peak throughput point (low interactivity) on GB300 NVL72. InferenceX, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, FP4, disaggregated Dynamo + vLLM, measured 2026-05-22. Counting: the source does not state whether tok/s/GPU counts output tokens only or input + output.

max_throughput_tok_s_user.note: Per-user speed at the peak-throughput point. Interactivity: output tokens per second per user (InferenceX x-axis). DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, FP4, measured 2026-05-22.

throughput_tok_s_gpu.note: At 27 tok/s/user (iso-interactivity table) on GB300 NVL72. InferenceX, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, FP4, disaggregated Dynamo + vLLM, measured 2026-05-22. Counting: the source does not state whether tok/s/GPU counts output tokens only or input + output.

interactivity_tok_s_user.note: The iso-interactivity operating point. Interactivity: output tokens per second per user (InferenceX x-axis). DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, FP4, measured 2026-05-22.

cost_per_m.note: At 27 tok/s/user on GB300 NVL72. Per M total (input + output) tokens: the article defines "cost per million total tokens" = $/GPU-hr x 1e6 / (3600 x tok/s/GPU). Measured 2026-05-22.

gpu_hour_usd.note: SemiAnalysis AI Cloud TCO model rental price used by the article.

per_gpu_gain_vs_gb200.note: "Up to 2.83x throughput per GPU vs GB200 NVL72 at iso-interactivity" (27 tok/s/user); attributed to 288 GB allowing EP 16 and larger prefill batches. Same tok/s/GPU counting caveat as throughput_tok_s_gpu.

max_throughput_tok_s_gpu.note: Peak throughput point (low interactivity) on GB200 NVL72. InferenceX, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, FP4, disaggregated Dynamo + vLLM, measured 2026-05-22. Counting: the source does not state whether tok/s/GPU counts output tokens only or input + output.

max_throughput_tok_s_user.note: Per-user speed at the peak-throughput point. Interactivity: output tokens per second per user (InferenceX x-axis). DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, FP4, measured 2026-05-22.

throughput_tok_s_gpu.note: At 27 tok/s/user (iso-interactivity table) on GB200 NVL72. InferenceX, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, FP4, disaggregated Dynamo + vLLM, measured 2026-05-22. Counting: the source does not state whether tok/s/GPU counts output tokens only or input + output.

interactivity_tok_s_user.note: The iso-interactivity operating point. Interactivity: output tokens per second per user (InferenceX x-axis). DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, FP4, measured 2026-05-22.

cost_per_m.note: At 27 tok/s/user on GB200 NVL72. Per M total (input + output) tokens: the article defines "cost per million total tokens" = $/GPU-hr x 1e6 / (3600 x tok/s/GPU). Measured 2026-05-22.

gpu_hour_usd.note: SemiAnalysis AI Cloud TCO model rental price used by the article.

entries.name: InferenceX: Kimi K2.5 on B200 (NVFP4) vs H200 (INT4)

cost_per_m_at_32.note: At 32 tok/s/user, B200 NVFP4, vLLM, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, run 2026-05-19. Counting: $/M = $/GPU-hr x 1e6 / (3600 x tok/s/GPU); the article does not say whether the throughput counts input tokens.

cost_per_m_at_90.note: At 90 tok/s/user (iso-interactivity table). Counting: the article does not say whether its tok/s/GPU (and so $/M) counts output tokens only or input + output.

cost_gain_vs_h200.note: Brief 04 §5 says 2.75-2.95x; the article (read 2026-10-07) says "2.71x-2.95x cheaper per million tokens than H200 INT4 in the 30-90 tok/s/user serving band" (2.75x is its 60 tok/s/user table point). The article's range is stored.

entries.name: LMSYS: DeepSeek-R1 long context on GB300 NVL72 (2026-02-19)

ttft_128k_s.note: DeepSeek-R1 NVFP4 on GB300, 128K-token prompt, chunked pipeline-parallel prefill (32K initial chunk, dynamic chunking), 1P/1D disaggregated on 8 GPUs.

mtp_per_user_gain_pct.note: Per-user output speed (TPS/User) rose from 23 to 43 with MTP; DeepSeek-R1 NVFP4 on GB300 NVL72, 128K input / 8K output, peak system throughput maintained.

names.note: The engines Dynamo 1.0 wraps as workers (brief 04 §7.1, §7.2). No verifiable market-share figure exists.

ga_date.note: Dynamo 1.0 general availability, announced at GTC.

kv_aware_router.value: Routes requests "to GPUs that already have the most relevant short-term memory from earlier steps"

cncf_sandbox_date.note: Accepted into CNCF Sandbox; brief 04 §7.1-7.2 via search snippet.

prefix_aware_routing.value: Prefix-cache-aware routing in its inference scheduler (Gateway API Inference Extension, "EPP")

tiers.value: HBM → host DRAM → storage (filesystem, S3-compatible via NIXL, peer-to-peer RDMA)

kv_events.value: Engines emit KV events so routers know what each replica holds

hbm_conversations.note: Qwen-35B on 2 x H100: up to 64 conversations fit in HBM.

cpu_offload_range.note: One source, not a conflict: between 64 and 128 conversations need CPU offload (Qwen-35B, 2 x H100).

storage_gain.note: Beyond 128 conversations, storage offload "more than doubled throughput" (Qwen-35B, 2 x H100).

bytes_factor.note: FP8 (e4m3) KV halves bytes per element vs BF16.

naive_niah_128k_pct.note: 128K needle-in-a-haystack accuracy with the naive FP8 implementation.

baseline_niah_128k_pct.note: 128K needle-in-a-haystack accuracy before the drop (BF16 baseline).

throughput_gain_llama_pct.note: Throughput gain on Llama (+4.8% on gpt-oss-20b).

breakeven_tokens.note: About 7K tokens; below this, FP8 KV is not worth it.

granularity.note: Design doc (read 2026-10-07): "We only cache full blocks"; block hash = hash(parent hash, token ids, extra keys such as LoRA ids).

eviction.note: The free queue's head is the least recently used block and is evicted first.

radix_attention.value: Cached KV kept in a radix tree keyed by token sequences, with LRU leaf eviction

capacity_gain_pct.note: One source, not a conflict: effective request capacity up 59%-498% under SLOs (FAST'25 coverage; paper arXiv 2407.00079 not re-fetched).

output_input_ratio.note: Output price per M output tokens is 5x the input price per M input tokens across current tiers.

batch_discount_pct.note: Batch API: 50% off both input and output.

flat_1m_context.note: Claude 4.6+ charge 1M-token context at the flat per-token price.

input_hit_usd_per_m.note: Off-peak, cache hit (3.3% of the miss price); no cache-write fee.

peak_mult.note: Peak rates are 2x off-peak; peak = 01-04 and 06-10 UTC, Mon-Fri.

entries.name: DeepSeek-V3 multi-token prediction as a drafter

acceptance_pct.note: One source, not a conflict: the DeepSeek-V3 report gives 85%-90% acceptance of the second (MTP-predicted) token.

tps_gain.note: About 1.8x tokens per second (per-user decode speed, as the report states it).

peak_speedup.note: Up to 6.5x vs vanilla decoding at small batch (abstract).

batch64_throughput_gain.note: Throughput gain at batch 64 in SGLang (abstract).

gain_vs_eagle3.note: Up to 1.69x over EAGLE-3 on B200.

exact_distribution.note: "Preserves the verifier model's output distribution exactly via rejection sampling."

parallel_drafters_note.value: Parallel drafters (P-EAGLE, DFlash, DSpark) are framed as the state of the art versus autoregressive EAGLE-3, and remove the need to retune speculation length as load changes

mainstream_note.value: Self-drafting heads (MTP, EAGLE-family) are the norm in open-model serving; separate draft models are a legacy option
mainstream_note.note: Brief 04 §4.3 "safe claim"; no share of traffic is published.

note.value: Prefill and decode run on different GPU pools and the KV cache moves between them; gains: no prefill-induced decode stalls, per-pool parallelism and batch size; costs: KV transfer and two pools to size
note.note: Brief 04 §6.1 summary of the technique; DistServe is the cited primary.

goodput_gain.note: Abstract (read 2026-10-07): "7.4x more requests or 12.6x tighter SLO" vs state-of-the-art systems. Brief 04 had it REPORTED via a summary.

slo_gain.note: Abstract: 12.6x tighter SLO (the alternative to 7.4x more requests).

throughput_gain.note: Abstract (read 2026-10-07): "1.4x higher throughput at 20% lower cost". Brief 04 had it REPORTED via a summary.

throughput_gain_same_cost.note: Abstract: "2.35x more throughput with the same cost and power budgets".

transports.value: NVLink, InfiniBand / RoCE RDMA, TCP fallback; used by Dynamo, llm-d, vLLM, Ray Serve LLM

disagg_moe_note.value: Disaggregation helps most for MoE with expert parallelism: one compute-bound prefill in the EP group delays the whole group's forward pass

wide_ep_note.value: Wide-EP = data-parallel attention + expert-parallel MoE ("a single set of experts are shared across ranks"); helpers DeepEP, DeepGEMM, EPLB, dual-batch overlap

entries.name: SGLang open reproduction of DeepSeek serving (May 2025)

output_gain_vs_tp16.note: Up to 5x output throughput over TP16; 96 H100 (12 nodes), PD + EP with 288 experts (256 + 32 redundant).

note.value: Weights to 4 bits, activations stay 16-bit: about 4x fewer bytes read in decode, but math still runs in 16-bit, so less useful at large compute-bound batches

r1_accuracy_loss_pct_max.note: Vendor claim (NVIDIA blog, 2025-06-24, read 2026-10-07): DeepSeek-R1-0528 FP8 → NVFP4 post-training quantization shows 1% or less accuracy loss on key tasks.
